title: Isaiah 14 — Israel restored and the taunt over the king of Babylon: the day star fallen from the heavens

verdicts.reasoning: kî yᵉraḥēm YHWH ʾeṯ-yaʿăqōḇ ... wᵉhinnîḥām ʿal-ʾaḏmāṯām wᵉnilwāh haggēr: 'settle them on their own ground', 'the sojourner will join himself' exact; ʾăḏāmāh 'ground' under the central entry.
ûlᵉqāḥûm ʿammîm ... wᵉhiṯnaḥălûm bêṯ-yiśrāʾēl ʿal ʾaḏmaṯ YHWH: 'possess them on the ground of YHWH', 'take captive those who were their captors' exact.
bᵉyôm hānîaḥ YHWH lᵉḵā mēʿoṣbᵉḵā ... ʾăšer ʿubbaḏ-bāḵ: 'the hard service with which you were made to serve' renders the Pual exactly.

citations: Ulrich & Flint, Qumran Cave 1.II: The Isaiah Scrolls (DJD 32, 2010), ad loc. (1QIsaᵃ מרהבה)
verdicts.reasoning: Disputed vs ASV 'parable'. māšāl introduces a mocking dirge, so 'taunt' (NRSV) is the contextual sense. madhēḇāh: MT kept with ASV's 'golden city'; the 1QIsaᵃ/LXX marhēḇāh reading adopted by NRSV/NJPS is fully reported. Defensible under the MT policy.
šāḇar YHWH maṭṭēh rᵉšāʿîm šēḇeṭ mōšᵉlîm: exact.
makkeh ʿammîm bᵉʿeḇrāh makkaṯ biltî sārāh ... murdāp̄ bᵉlî ḥāśāḵ: 'unceasing stroke', 'persecution none restrained' exact.
nāḥāh šāqᵉṭāh kol-hāʾāreṣ pāṣᵉḥû rinnāh: exact.
gam-bᵉrôšîm śāmᵉḥû lᵉḵā ... lōʾ-yaʿăleh hakkōrēṯ ʿālênû: quoted speech of the trees kept; exact.
šᵉʾôl mittaḥaṯ rāḡᵉzāh lᵉḵā ... ʿôrēr lᵉḵā rᵉp̄āʾîm kol-ʿattûḏê ʾāreṣ: 'She'ol', 'the shades', 'leaders of the earth' (lit. 'he-goats') are standard.
gam-ʾattāh ḥullêṯā ḵāmônû ʾēlênû nimšāltā: exact.
hûraḏ šᵉʾôl gᵉʾôneḵā hemyaṯ nᵉḇāleḵā ... rimmāh ... tôlēʿāh: exact.

citations: Day, Yahweh and the Gods and Goddesses of Canaan (2000)
verdicts.reasoning: Disputed. ʾêḵ nāp̄altā miššāmayim hêlēl ben-šāḥar ... ḥôlēš ʿal-gôyim: common nouns 'day star, son of the dawn' (ASV/NRSV), no 'Lucifer'; 'from the heavens' is the divine-realm register, matching v. 13. Not lens-driven; the Lucifer reception and the Ugaritic background are in commentary.

citations: NRSV “the heights of Zaphon”; NJPS “the summit of Zaphon”
verdicts.reasoning: Canon-cited, disputed vs ASV 'north'. haššāmayim ʾeʿĕleh mimmaʿal lᵉḵôḵᵉḇê-ʾēl ... bᵉhar-môʿēḏ bᵉyarkᵉṯê ṣāp̄ôn: 'Zaphon' as the divine mountain's name follows NRSV/NJPS and the consensus. 'stars of God' and 'mount of assembly' standard. Lens check: the line does not identify the speaker (canon: human scientists), and the reception note keeps to the text's 'king of Babylon'.
Canon-cited. ʾeʿĕleh ʿal-bāmŏṯê ʿāḇ ʾeddammeh lᵉʿelyôn: 'the heights of the clouds', 'the Most High' (also the canon's 'Très-Haut'). Exact.
ʾaḵ ʾel-šᵉʾôl tûrāḏ ʾel-yarkᵉṯê-ḇôr: 'far reaches of the pit' mirrors v. 13 literally; exact.
rōʾeyḵā ʾēleyḵā yašgîḥû ... hăzeh hāʾîš margîz hāʾāreṣ: exact.

Canon-cited. śām tēḇēl kammiḏbār wᵉʿārāyw hārās ʾăsîrāyw lōʾ-p̄āṯaḥ bāyᵉṯāh: the clause stays inside the onlookers' question, as the Hebrew syntax requires; 'did not let his prisoners go home' (NRSV) is exact. Reception note accurate.
kol-malḵê ḡôyim kullām šāḵᵉḇû ḇᵉḵāḇôḏ ʾîš bᵉḇêṯô: exact.
hušlaḵtā miqqiḇrᵉḵā kᵉnēṣer niṯʿāḇ lᵉḇûš hărūḡîm ... kᵉp̄eḡer mûḇās: 'clothed with the slain' (ASV), 'stones of the pit' exact.
lōʾ-ṯēḥaḏ ʾittām biqḇûrāh kî-ʾarṣᵉḵā šiḥattā ... lōʾ-yiqqārēʾ lᵉʿôlām zeraʿ mᵉrēʿîm: territorial 'your land' correct; exact.
hāḵînû lᵉḇānāyw maṭbēaḥ ... ûmālᵉʾû p̄ᵉnê-ṯēḇēl ʿārîm: exact.
wᵉqamtî ʿălêhem nᵉʾum YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ ... šēm ûšᵉʾār wᵉnîn wāneḵeḏ: exact.
lᵉmôraš qippōḏ ... bᵉmaṭʾăṭēʾ hašmēḏ: 'porcupine' (ASV; NRSV 'hedgehog'), 'broom of destruction' exact.
nišbaʿ YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ ... ʾim-lōʾ kaʾăšer dimmîṯî kēn hāyāṯāh: oath formula rendered 'Surely'; exact.
lišbōr ʾaššûr bᵉʾarṣî ... wᵉsār mēʿălêhem ʿullô: exact; 'my land' territorial.
zōʾṯ hāʿēṣāh hayyᵉʿûṣāh ʿal-kol-hāʾāreṣ: exact.
kî-YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ yāʿāṣ ûmî yāp̄ēr: exact.
Disputed vs ASV 'burden'. bišnaṯ-môṯ hammeleḵ ʾāḥāz hāyāh hammaśśāʾ hazzeh: heading noun, 'oracle'; consistent with 13:1.
miššōreš nāḥāš yēṣēʾ ṣep̄aʿ ûp̄iryô śārāp̄ mᵉʿôp̄ēp̄: in a series of snakes śārāp̄ is a serpent; 'a fiery flying serpent' (ASV) is correct and the context rule against 6:2 is sound.

verdicts.reasoning: wᵉhēmattî ... ûšᵉʾērîṯēḵ yahărōḡ: MT's third person kept, 1QIsaᵃ first person reported. Under the MT policy, defensible.
hêlîlî šaʿar zaʿăqî-ʿîr ... miṣṣāp̄ôn ʿāšān bāʾ wᵉʾên bôḏēḏ bᵉmôʿāḏāyw: here ṣāp̄ôn is the compass point 'north'; exact.

paragraphs.text: כִּי֩ יְרַחֵ֨ם יְהוָ֜ה אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹ֗ב וּבָחַ֥ר עוֹד֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהִנִּיחָ֖ם עַל־אַדְמָתָ֑ם וְנִלְוָ֤ה הַגֵּר֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְנִסְפְּח֖וּ עַל־בֵּ֥ית יַעֲקֹֽב׃

i18n.en: For YHWH will have compassion on Jacob and will again choose Israel, and will settle them on their own ground; and the sojourner will join himself to them, and they will attach themselves to the house of Jacob.
i18n.he: כִּי֩ יְרַחֵ֨ם יְהוָ֜ה אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹ֗ב וּבָחַ֥ר עוֹד֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהִנִּיחָ֖ם עַל־אַדְמָתָ֑ם וְנִלְוָ֤ה הַגֵּר֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְנִסְפְּח֖וּ עַל־בֵּ֥ית יַעֲקֹֽב׃

paragraphs.text: וּלְקָח֣וּם עַמִּים֮ וֶהֱבִיא֣וּם אֶל־מְקוֹמָם֒ וְהִֽתְנַחֲל֣וּם בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עַ֚ל אַדְמַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה לַעֲבָדִ֖ים וְלִשְׁפָח֑וֹת וְהָיוּ֙ שֹׁבִ֣ים לְשֹֽׁבֵיהֶ֔ם וְרָד֖וּ בְּנֹגְשֵׂיהֶֽם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And peoples will take them and bring them to their place, and the house of Israel will possess them on the ground of YHWH as menservants and maidservants; they will take captive those who were their captors, and they will rule over their oppressors.
i18n.he: וּלְקָח֣וּם עַמִּים֮ וֶהֱבִיא֣וּם אֶל־מְקוֹמָם֒ וְהִֽתְנַחֲל֣וּם בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עַ֚ל אַדְמַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה לַעֲבָדִ֖ים וְלִשְׁפָח֑וֹת וְהָיוּ֙ שֹׁבִ֣ים לְשֹֽׁבֵיהֶ֔ם וְרָד֖וּ בְּנֹגְשֵׂיהֶֽם׃ (ס)

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ מֵֽעָצְבְּךָ֖ וּמֵרָגְזֶ֑ךָ וּמִן־הָעֲבֹדָ֥ה הַקָּשָׁ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֻבַּד־בָּֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And it shall be, on the day that YHWH gives you rest from your pain and from your turmoil and from the hard service with which you were made to serve,
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ מֵֽעָצְבְּךָ֖ וּמֵרָגְזֶ֑ךָ וּמִן־הָעֲבֹדָ֥ה הַקָּשָׁ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֻבַּד־בָּֽךְ׃

paragraphs.text: וְנָשָׂ֜אתָ הַמָּשָׁ֥ל הַזֶּ֛ה עַל־מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל וְאָמָ֑רְתָּ אֵ֚יךְ שָׁבַ֣ת נֹגֵ֔שׂ שָׁבְתָ֖ה מַדְהֵבָֽה׃

i18n.en: that you will take up this taunt against the king of Babylon, and say: “How the oppressor has ceased, the golden city ceased!
i18n.he: וְנָשָׂ֜אתָ הַמָּשָׁ֥ל הַזֶּ֛ה עַל־מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל וְאָמָ֑רְתָּ אֵ֚יךְ שָׁבַ֣ת נֹגֵ֔שׂ שָׁבְתָ֖ה מַדְהֵבָֽה׃

notes.official: *māšāl* covers proverb, parable and taunt-song. Here it introduces a mocking dirge over a dead tyrant, so the line has “taunt” (NRSV; NJPS “song of scorn”); in modern English ASV’s “parable” means an instructive story. *madhēḇāh* is unexplained in MT. ASV’s “the golden city” derives it from Aramaic *dᵉhaḇ* “gold.” The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaᵃ) reads מרהבה *marhēḇāh* “onslaught, arrogance” (√*rhb*), the LXX supports it, and NRSV and NJPS adopt it (“how his insolence has ceased”). Under the textual policy of this translation the line keeps MT with ASV’s interpretation, and the Qumran reading is given here as the one most modern versions follow (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: שָׁבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה מַטֵּ֣ה רְשָׁעִ֑ים שֵׁ֖בֶט מֹשְׁלִֽים׃

i18n.en: YHWH has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of rulers,
i18n.he: שָׁבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה מַטֵּ֣ה רְשָׁעִ֑ים שֵׁ֖בֶט מֹשְׁלִֽים׃

paragraphs.text: מַכֶּ֤ה עַמִּים֙ בְּעֶבְרָ֔ה מַכַּ֖ת בִּלְתִּ֣י סָרָ֑ה רֹדֶ֤ה בָאַף֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם מֻרְדָּ֖ף בְּלִ֥י חָשָֽׂךְ׃

i18n.en: that struck peoples in wrath with an unceasing stroke, that ruled nations in anger with a persecution none restrained.
i18n.he: מַכֶּ֤ה עַמִּים֙ בְּעֶבְרָ֔ה מַכַּ֖ת בִּלְתִּ֣י סָרָ֑ה רֹדֶ֤ה בָאַף֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם מֻרְדָּ֖ף בְּלִ֥י חָשָֽׂךְ׃

paragraphs.text: נָ֥חָה שָׁקְטָ֖ה כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ פָּצְח֖וּ רִנָּֽה׃

i18n.en: The whole earth is at rest and is quiet; they break forth into singing.
i18n.he: נָ֥חָה שָׁקְטָ֖ה כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ פָּצְח֖וּ רִנָּֽה׃

paragraphs.text: גַּם־בְּרוֹשִׁ֛ים שָׂמְח֥וּ לְךָ֖ אַרְזֵ֣י לְבָנ֑וֹן מֵאָ֣ז שָׁכַ֔בְתָּ לֹֽא־יַעֲלֶ֥ה הַכֹּרֵ֖ת עָלֵֽינוּ׃

i18n.en: Even the cypresses rejoice over you, the cedars of Lebanon: ‘Since you were laid low, no woodcutter comes up against us.’
i18n.he: גַּם־בְּרוֹשִׁ֛ים שָׂמְח֥וּ לְךָ֖ אַרְזֵ֣י לְבָנ֑וֹן מֵאָ֣ז שָׁכַ֔בְתָּ לֹֽא־יַעֲלֶ֥ה הַכֹּרֵ֖ת עָלֵֽינוּ׃

paragraphs.text: שְׁא֗וֹל מִתַּ֛חַת רָגְזָ֥ה לְךָ֖ לִקְרַ֣את בּוֹאֶ֑ךָ עוֹרֵ֨ר לְךָ֤ רְפָאִים֙ כָּל־עַתּ֣וּדֵי אָ֔רֶץ הֵקִים֙ מִכִּסְאוֹתָ֔ם כֹּ֖ל מַלְכֵ֥י גוֹיִֽם׃

i18n.en: She'ol beneath is stirred up for you, to meet you at your coming; it rouses the shades for you, all the leaders of the earth; it raises from their thrones all the kings of the nations.
i18n.he: שְׁא֗וֹל מִתַּ֛חַת רָגְזָ֥ה לְךָ֖ לִקְרַ֣את בּוֹאֶ֑ךָ עוֹרֵ֨ר לְךָ֤ רְפָאִים֙ כָּל־עַתּ֣וּדֵי אָ֔רֶץ הֵקִים֙ מִכִּסְאוֹתָ֔ם כֹּ֖ל מַלְכֵ֥י גוֹיִֽם׃

notes.official: *šᵉʾôl* is transliterated “She’ol” under the central entry, and the *rᵉp̄āʾîm* are “the shades,” the dead in the underworld, under the overlay entry written for 26:14, 19. The dead kings rise from their thrones to greet the newcomer, a scene that inverts the royal reception of a living king.

paragraphs.text: כֻּלָּ֣ם יַֽעֲנ֔וּ וְיֹאמְר֖וּ אֵלֶ֑יךָ גַּם־אַתָּ֛ה חֻלֵּ֥יתָ כָמ֖וֹנוּ אֵלֵ֥ינוּ נִמְשָֽׁלְתָּ׃

i18n.en: All of them will answer and say to you: ‘You too have become weak as we are; you have become like us!’
i18n.he: כֻּלָּ֣ם יַֽעֲנ֔וּ וְיֹאמְר֖וּ אֵלֶ֑יךָ גַּם־אַתָּ֛ה חֻלֵּ֥יתָ כָמ֖וֹנוּ אֵלֵ֥ינוּ נִמְשָֽׁלְתָּ׃

paragraphs.text: הוּרַ֥ד שְׁא֛וֹל גְּאוֹנֶ֖ךָ הֶמְיַ֣ת נְבָלֶ֑יךָ תַּחְתֶּ֙יךָ֙ יֻצַּ֣ע רִמָּ֔ה וּמְכַסֶּ֖יךָ תּוֹלֵעָֽה׃

i18n.en: Your pomp is brought down to She'ol, the sound of your harps; beneath you maggots are spread out, and worms are your covering.
i18n.he: הוּרַ֥ד שְׁא֛וֹל גְּאוֹנֶ֖ךָ הֶמְיַ֣ת נְבָלֶ֑יךָ תַּחְתֶּ֙יךָ֙ יֻצַּ֣ע רִמָּ֔ה וּמְכַסֶּ֖יךָ תּוֹלֵעָֽה׃

paragraphs.text: אֵ֛יךְ נָפַ֥לְתָּ מִשָּׁמַ֖יִם הֵילֵ֣ל בֶּן־שָׁ֑חַר נִגְדַּ֣עְתָּ לָאָ֔רֶץ חוֹלֵ֖שׁ עַל־גּוֹיִֽם׃

i18n.en: How you have fallen from the heavens, O day star, son of the dawn! How you are cut down to the ground, you who laid the nations low!
i18n.he: אֵ֛יךְ נָפַ֥לְתָּ מִשָּׁמַ֖יִם הֵילֵ֣ל בֶּן־שָׁ֑חַר נִגְדַּ֣עְתָּ לָאָ֔רֶץ חוֹלֵ֖שׁ עַל־גּוֹיִֽם׃

notes.official:
*hêlēl ben-šāḥar* is “O day star, son of the dawn” (ASV “day-star, son of the morning”; NRSV “Day Star, son of Dawn”). *hêlēl* is from *hll* “shine,” and the “shining one” is usually identified as the morning star, Venus. The LXX has *heōsphoros* “dawn-bringer” and the Vulgate *lucifer* “light-bearer,” whence the KJV’s “Lucifer” and the later identification with a fallen angel. That identification belongs to the reception history, not the Hebrew. *šaḥar* “dawn” is also a deity at Ugarit (*Šaḥaru*, KTU 1.23), so the phrase may once have been a pair of divine names. The line keeps common nouns, because the passage taunts the king of Babylon (v. 4) with a mythic image and does not narrate the myth itself (Wildberger, *Isaiah 13–27*; Day, *Yahweh and the Gods and Goddesses of Canaan*, 2000).

*min-haš-šāmayim* is “from the heavens.” The fall in v. 12 reverses the ascent vowed in v. 13, and v. 13 places the throne among “the stars of God” and the “mount of assembly,” the realm of the divine council. The central *šāmayim* register rule sends that realm to “heaven(s),” so both verses use the divine-realm register (overlay `helel-zaphon-elyon-taunt-isaiah-14`).

paragraphs.text: וְאַתָּ֞ה אָמַ֤רְתָּ בִֽלְבָבְךָ֙ הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם אֶֽעֱלֶ֔ה מִמַּ֥עַל לְכֽוֹכְבֵי־אֵ֖ל אָרִ֣ים כִּסְאִ֑י וְאֵשֵׁ֥ב בְּהַר־מוֹעֵ֖ד בְּיַרְכְּתֵ֥י צָפֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: And you said in your heart: ‘I will ascend to the heavens; above the stars of God I will raise my throne; and I will sit on the mount of assembly, in the far reaches of Zaphon;
i18n.he: וְאַתָּ֞ה אָמַ֤רְתָּ בִֽלְבָבְךָ֙ הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם אֶֽעֱלֶ֔ה מִמַּ֥עַל לְכֽוֹכְבֵי־אֵ֖ל אָרִ֣ים כִּסְאִ֑י וְאֵשֵׁ֥ב בְּהַר־מוֹעֵ֖ד בְּיַרְכְּתֵ֥י צָפֽוֹן׃

notes.official:
Three phrases of the vow come from the West-Semitic picture of the divine mountain. *kôḵᵉḇê-ʾēl* is “the stars of God” (ASV, NRSV, NJPS). *ʾēl* may here be the high god El himself, which is the reading cited in the central `kokhvei-boqer` rationale; the line keeps the book’s “God” for *ʾēl*. *har-môʿēḏ* is “the mount of assembly,” the meeting-place of the divine council. *yarkᵉṯê ṣāp̄ôn* is “the far reaches of Zaphon”: *ṣāp̄ôn* is the name of the divine mountain, Ugaritic *Ṣapunu* (Jebel el-Aqraʿ), the seat of Baʿlu, before it became the common word for “north.” NRSV (“the heights of Zaphon”) and NJPS (“the summit of Zaphon”) give the name, and the line follows them in place of ASV’s “the uttermost parts of the north” (Clifford, *The Cosmic Mountain*, 1972; central `mount-sapunu-tsafon-cosmic-mountain-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible`). *yarkᵉṯê* is “the far reaches” both here and in v. 15 (“the far reaches of the pit”), so the matching height and depth stay visible in English.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes v. 13 (“I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God”) and reads the vow as that of human scientists who had gained enough knowledge to set out for the creators’ planet. It identifies them with the men destroyed at Sodom and Gomorrah. The line renders the vow with the standard vocabulary of the Hebrew myth, and the apparatus carries no identification of the speaker beyond the text’s own “king of Babylon” (v. 4).

paragraphs.text: אֶעֱלֶ֖ה עַל־בָּ֣מֳתֵי עָ֑ב אֶדַּמֶּ֖ה לְעֶלְיֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will make myself like the Most High.’
i18n.he: אֶעֱלֶ֖ה עַל־בָּ֣מֳתֵי עָ֑ב אֶדַּמֶּ֖ה לְעֶלְיֽוֹן׃

notes.official:
*ʾeddammeh lᵉʿelyôn* “I will make myself like the Most High.” Standalone *ʿelyôn* is rendered “the Most High,” the standard rendering, which is also the French canon’s “le Très-Haut.” The central `el-elyon` entry transliterates “El Elyon” for the compound and is not extended to the bare title. *bāmŏṯê ʿāḇ* is “the heights of the clouds” (ASV; NRSV “the tops of the clouds”).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The canon quotes v. 14 (“I will ascend above the heights of the cloud, I will be like the Most High”) and comments that the destruction prevented man from equaling the creators, “the Most High.” The line renders *ʿelyôn* by the standard title.

paragraphs.text: אַ֧ךְ אֶל־שְׁא֛וֹל תּוּרָ֖ד אֶל־יַרְכְּתֵי־בֽוֹר׃

i18n.en: Yet you are brought down to She'ol, to the far reaches of the pit.
i18n.he: אַ֧ךְ אֶל־שְׁא֛וֹל תּוּרָ֖ד אֶל־יַרְכְּתֵי־בֽוֹר׃

notes.official: The fall answers the vow word for word: the one who would sit “in the far reaches of Zaphon” (v. 13) is brought down “to the far reaches of the pit” (*yarkᵉṯê-ḇôr*). *bôr* is “pit” under the central `bor-pit-cistern-dry-water-shaft` entry, here a synonym for She’ol, as at 14:19 and 38:18.

paragraphs.text: רֹאֶ֙יךָ֙ אֵלֶ֣יךָ יַשְׁגִּ֔יחוּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ יִתְבּוֹנָ֑נוּ הֲזֶ֤ה הָאִישׁ֙ מַרְגִּ֣יז הָאָ֔רֶץ מַרְעִ֖ישׁ מַמְלָכֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: Those who see you will stare at you, they will ponder over you: ‘Is this the man who made the earth tremble, who shook kingdoms,
i18n.he: רֹאֶ֙יךָ֙ אֵלֶ֣יךָ יַשְׁגִּ֔יחוּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ יִתְבּוֹנָ֑נוּ הֲזֶ֤ה הָאִישׁ֙ מַרְגִּ֣יז הָאָ֔רֶץ מַרְעִ֖ישׁ מַמְלָכֽוֹת׃

paragraphs.text: שָׂ֥ם תֵּבֵ֛ל כַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר וְעָרָ֣יו הָרָ֑ס אֲסִירָ֖יו לֹא־פָ֥תַח בָּֽיְתָה׃

i18n.en: who made the world like a wilderness and overthrew its cities, who did not let his prisoners go home?’
i18n.he: שָׂ֥ם תֵּבֵ֛ל כַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר וְעָרָ֣יו הָרָ֑ס אֲסִירָ֖יו לֹא־פָ֥תַח בָּֽיְתָה׃

notes.official: **Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The canon quotes the first clause of v. 17 (“He made the world as a wilderness”) as part of its Sodom-and-Gomorrah reading of 14:13–17 (see the note at v. 13). In the Hebrew the clause belongs to the onlookers’ question about the fallen king, “Is this the man who … made the world like a wilderness?” (vv. 16–17), and the line renders it so. *tēḇēl* is “the world,” the inhabited earth.

paragraphs.text: כָּל־מַלְכֵ֥י גוֹיִ֖ם כֻּלָּ֑ם שָׁכְב֥וּ בְכָב֖וֹד אִ֥ישׁ בְּבֵיתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: All the kings of the nations, all of them, lie in glory, each in his own house;
i18n.he: כָּל־מַלְכֵ֥י גוֹיִ֖ם כֻּלָּ֑ם שָׁכְב֥וּ בְכָב֖וֹד אִ֥ישׁ בְּבֵיתֽוֹ׃

paragraphs.text: וְאַתָּ֞ה הָשְׁלַ֤כְתָּ מִֽקִּבְרְךָ֙ כְּנֵ֣צֶר נִתְעָ֔ב לְב֥וּשׁ הֲרֻגִ֖ים מְטֹ֣עֲנֵי חָ֑רֶב יוֹרְדֵ֥י אֶל־אַבְנֵי־ב֖וֹר כְּפֶ֥גֶר מוּבָֽס׃

i18n.en: but you are cast out away from your grave like a loathed branch, clothed with the slain, those pierced by the sword, who go down to the stones of the pit, like a corpse trampled underfoot.
i18n.he: וְאַתָּ֞ה הָשְׁלַ֤כְתָּ מִֽקִּבְרְךָ֙ כְּנֵ֣צֶר נִתְעָ֔ב לְב֥וּשׁ הֲרֻגִ֖ים מְטֹ֣עֲנֵי חָ֑רֶב יוֹרְדֵ֥י אֶל־אַבְנֵי־ב֖וֹר כְּפֶ֥גֶר מוּבָֽס׃

paragraphs.text: לֹֽא־תֵחַ֤ד אִתָּם֙ בִּקְבוּרָ֔ה כִּֽי־אַרְצְךָ֥ שִׁחַ֖תָּ עַמְּךָ֣ הָרָ֑גְתָּ לֹֽא־יִקָּרֵ֥א לְעוֹלָ֖ם זֶ֥רַע מְרֵעִֽים׃

i18n.en: You will not be joined with them in burial, because you have destroyed your land, you have slain your people. The seed of evildoers will not be named forever.
i18n.he: לֹֽא־תֵחַ֤ד אִתָּם֙ בִּקְבוּרָ֔ה כִּֽי־אַרְצְךָ֥ שִׁחַ֖תָּ עַמְּךָ֣ הָרָ֑גְתָּ לֹֽא־יִקָּרֵ֥א לְעוֹלָ֖ם זֶ֥רַע מְרֵעִֽים׃

paragraphs.text: הָכִ֧ינוּ לְבָנָ֛יו מַטְבֵּ֖חַ בַּעֲוֺ֣ן אֲבוֹתָ֑ם בַּל־יָקֻ֙מוּ֙ וְיָ֣רְשׁוּ אָ֔רֶץ וּמָלְא֥וּ פְנֵֽי־תֵבֵ֖ל עָרִֽים׃

i18n.en: Prepare a slaughtering-place for his sons because of the iniquity of their fathers, lest they rise and possess the earth, and fill the face of the world with cities.”
i18n.he: הָכִ֧ינוּ לְבָנָ֛יו מַטְבֵּ֖חַ בַּעֲוֺ֣ן אֲבוֹתָ֑ם בַּל־יָקֻ֙מוּ֙ וְיָ֣רְשׁוּ אָ֔רֶץ וּמָלְא֥וּ פְנֵֽי־תֵבֵ֖ל עָרִֽים׃

paragraphs.text: וְקַמְתִּ֣י עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וְהִכְרַתִּ֨י לְבָבֶ֜ל שֵׁ֥ם וּשְׁאָ֛ר וְנִ֥ין וָנֶ֖כֶד נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And I will rise up against them, says YHWH of hosts, and I will cut off from Babylon name and remnant, offspring and posterity, says YHWH.
i18n.he: וְקַמְתִּ֣י עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וְהִכְרַתִּ֨י לְבָבֶ֜ל שֵׁ֥ם וּשְׁאָ֛ר וְנִ֥ין וָנֶ֖כֶד נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

paragraphs.text: וְשַׂמְתִּ֛יהָ לְמוֹרַ֥שׁ קִפֹּ֖ד וְאַגְמֵי־מָ֑יִם וְטֵֽאטֵאתִ֙יהָ֙ בְּמַטְאֲטֵ֣א הַשְׁמֵ֔ד נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And I will make it a possession of the porcupine, and pools of water, and I will sweep it with the broom of destruction, says YHWH of hosts.
i18n.he: וְשַׂמְתִּ֛יהָ לְמוֹרַ֥שׁ קִפֹּ֖ד וְאַגְמֵי־מָ֑יִם וְטֵֽאטֵאתִ֙יהָ֙ בְּמַטְאֲטֵ֣א הַשְׁמֵ֔ד נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ (פ)

paragraphs.text: נִשְׁבַּ֛ע יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם־לֹ֞א כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּמִּ֙יתִי֙ כֵּ֣ן הָיָ֔תָה וְכַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָעַ֖צְתִּי הִ֥יא תָקֽוּם׃

i18n.en: YHWH of hosts has sworn, saying: “Surely, as I have planned, so it shall come to pass, and as I have purposed, so it shall stand:
i18n.he: נִשְׁבַּ֛ע יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם־לֹ֞א כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּמִּ֙יתִי֙ כֵּ֣ן הָיָ֔תָה וְכַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָעַ֖צְתִּי הִ֥יא תָקֽוּם׃

paragraphs.text: לִשְׁבֹּ֤ר אַשּׁוּר֙ בְּאַרְצִ֔י וְעַל־הָרַ֖י אֲבוּסֶ֑נּוּ וְסָ֤ר מֵֽעֲלֵיהֶם֙ עֻלּ֔וֹ וְסֻ֨בֳּל֔וֹ מֵעַ֥ל שִׁכְמ֖וֹ יָסֽוּר׃

i18n.en: to break Assyria in my land, and upon my mountains to trample him; then his yoke shall depart from them, and his burden shall depart from their shoulder.”
i18n.he: לִשְׁבֹּ֤ר אַשּׁוּר֙ בְּאַרְצִ֔י וְעַל־הָרַ֖י אֲבוּסֶ֑נּוּ וְסָ֤ר מֵֽעֲלֵיהֶם֙ עֻלּ֔וֹ וְסֻ֨בֳּל֔וֹ מֵעַ֥ל שִׁכְמ֖וֹ יָסֽוּר׃

paragraphs.text: זֹ֛את הָעֵצָ֥ה הַיְּעוּצָ֖ה עַל־כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְזֹ֛את הַיָּ֥ד הַנְּטוּיָ֖ה עַל־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

i18n.en: This is the purpose that is purposed concerning the whole earth, and this is the hand that is stretched out over all the nations.
i18n.he: זֹ֛את הָעֵצָ֥ה הַיְּעוּצָ֖ה עַל־כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְזֹ֛את הַיָּ֥ד הַנְּטוּיָ֖ה עַל־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת יָעָ֖ץ וּמִ֣י יָפֵ֑ר וְיָד֥וֹ הַנְּטוּיָ֖ה וּֽמִ֥י יְשִׁיבֶֽנָּה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: For YHWH of hosts has purposed, and who will annul it? His hand is stretched out, and who will turn it back?
i18n.he: כִּֽי־יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת יָעָ֖ץ וּמִ֣י יָפֵ֑ר וְיָד֥וֹ הַנְּטוּיָ֖ה וּֽמִ֥י יְשִׁיבֶֽנָּה׃ (פ)

paragraphs.text: בִּשְׁנַת־מ֖וֹת הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָחָ֑ז הָיָ֖ה הַמַּשָּׂ֥א הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: In the year that King Ahaz died came this oracle:
i18n.he: בִּשְׁנַת־מ֖וֹת הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָחָ֑ז הָיָ֖ה הַמַּשָּׂ֥א הַזֶּֽה׃

paragraphs.text: אַֽל־תִּשְׂמְחִ֤י פְלֶ֙שֶׁת֙ כֻּלֵּ֔ךְ כִּ֥י נִשְׁבַּ֖ר שֵׁ֣בֶט מַכֵּ֑ךְ כִּֽי־מִשֹּׁ֤רֶשׁ נָחָשׁ֙ יֵ֣צֵא צֶ֔פַע וּפִרְי֖וֹ שָׂרָ֥ף מְעוֹפֵֽף׃

i18n.en: Do not rejoice, Philistia, all of you, that the rod that struck you is broken; for from the serpent's root will come forth an adder, and its fruit will be a fiery flying serpent.
i18n.he: אַֽל־תִּשְׂמְחִ֤י פְלֶ֙שֶׁת֙ כֻּלֵּ֔ךְ כִּ֥י נִשְׁבַּ֖ר שֵׁ֣בֶט מַכֵּ֑ךְ כִּֽי־מִשֹּׁ֤רֶשׁ נָחָשׁ֙ יֵ֣צֵא צֶ֔פַע וּפִרְי֖וֹ שָׂרָ֥ף מְעוֹפֵֽף׃

notes.official: *śārāp̄ mᵉʿôp̄ēp̄* stands in a series of snakes: *nāḥāš* “serpent,” *ṣep̄aʿ* “adder,” *śārāp̄*. Here, as at Num 21:6, Deut 8:15 and Isa 30:6, *śārāp̄* is a venomous snake, and the line has “a fiery flying serpent” (ASV; NRSV “flying fiery serpent”). The six-winged throne-attendants of Isa 6:2 are the same lexeme, transliterated “seraphim” there because they act as courtiers with faces, feet and voices. The overlay `seraphim-burning-ones-isaiah` now records that context decides between the two, and the shared root *śrp* “burn” is the link (Joines, *JBL* 86 [1967] 410–415).

paragraphs.text: וְרָעוּ֙ בְּכוֹרֵ֣י דַלִּ֔ים וְאֶבְיוֹנִ֖ים לָבֶ֣טַח יִרְבָּ֑צוּ וְהֵמַתִּ֤י בָֽרָעָב֙ שָׁרְשֵׁ֔ךְ וּשְׁאֵרִיתֵ֖ךְ יַהֲרֹֽג׃

i18n.en: And the firstborn of the poor will graze, and the needy will lie down in safety; but I will kill your root with famine, and your remnant he will slay.
i18n.he: וְרָעוּ֙ בְּכוֹרֵ֣י דַלִּ֔ים וְאֶבְיוֹנִ֖ים לָבֶ֣טַח יִרְבָּ֑צוּ וְהֵמַתִּ֤י בָֽרָעָב֙ שָׁרְשֵׁ֔ךְ וּשְׁאֵרִיתֵ֖ךְ יַהֲרֹֽג׃

notes.official: MT *yahărōḡ* “he will slay” has no expressed subject (the adder of v. 29, or the enemy from the north of v. 31) and follows the first-person *wᵉhēmattî* “I will kill.” The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaᵃ) reads אהרוג *ʾahărōḡ* “I will slay,” which keeps the first person, and some modern versions adopt it. The line keeps MT under the translation’s textual policy.

paragraphs.text: הֵילִ֤ילִֽי שַׁ֙עַר֙ זַֽעֲקִי־עִ֔יר נָמ֖וֹג פְּלֶ֣שֶׁת כֻּלֵּ֑ךְ כִּ֤י מִצָּפוֹן֙ עָשָׁ֣ן בָּ֔א וְאֵ֥ין בּוֹדֵ֖ד בְּמוֹעָדָֽיו׃

i18n.en: Wail, O gate! Cry out, O city! Melt away, Philistia, all of you! For smoke comes out of the north, and there is no straggler in his ranks.
i18n.he: הֵילִ֤ילִֽי שַׁ֙עַר֙ זַֽעֲקִי־עִ֔יר נָמ֖וֹג פְּלֶ֣שֶׁת כֻּלֵּ֑ךְ כִּ֤י מִצָּפוֹן֙ עָשָׁ֣ן בָּ֔א וְאֵ֥ין בּוֹדֵ֖ד בְּמוֹעָדָֽיו׃

paragraphs.text: וּמַֽה־יַּעֲנֶ֖ה מַלְאֲכֵי־ג֑וֹי כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ יִסַּ֣ד צִיּ֔וֹן וּבָ֥הּ יֶחֱס֖וּ עֲנִיֵּ֥י עַמּֽוֹ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And what will one answer the messengers of the nation? That YHWH has founded Zion, and in her the afflicted of his people will take refuge.
i18n.he: וּמַֽה־יַּעֲנֶ֖ה מַלְאֲכֵי־ג֑וֹי כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ יִסַּ֣ד צִיּ֔וֹן וּבָ֥הּ יֶחֱס֖וּ עֲנִיֵּ֥י עַמּֽוֹ׃ (ס)
